title: Vulnerability management program and identification coverage
status_rationale: SOC2-016 directs that vulnerability programs record findings, prioritization, fixes, exceptions and retest evidence, and SEC-SUPPLY-001 proposes vulnerability checks on dependencies; neither is implemented and no production service exists.
target_answer: Echelon operates an inventory-driven vulnerability management program: every deployed component is derived from build SBOMs and deployment manifests and continuously matched against OSV, vendor advisories (.NET, PostgreSQL, base images, cloud provider bulletins) and CISA KEV; components missing from the inventory raise gaps; every finding enters one register with lifecycle timestamps; and coverage, aging and exception metrics are reported with raw denominators.
current_practice: Not established. No vulnerability management policy, register or scanning workflow was located in Echelon repositories reviewed (no CodeQL, dependency or vulnerability scanning workflow found in Praxis or product repositories).
intended_practice: Adopt a vulnerability management procedure under the Secure Construction Standard, implement SBOM-fed SCA in CI, and build the register as a byproduct of the pipeline before Unbound handles real data.
provable: Nothing operational. Only the proposed Standard and Unbound directive text exist.
customer_statement: Echelon has defined, but not yet implemented, a vulnerability management design for Unbound. Unbound is not yet in production; we can share the proposed design and will provide operating evidence once the service is live.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
residual_risks: Advisory coverage for F# and less common NuGet packages may be sparse; absence of findings is not absence of vulnerabilities.
open_questions: Which hosting provider and managed services will Unbound use, and what vulnerability information do they provide?
Who is the accountable owner of the vulnerability program?

title: Risk-based vulnerability prioritization (CVSS v4, EPSS, KEV, reachability, VEX)
status_rationale: No prioritization method is documented anywhere in Echelon sources; the target is a recommendation of this research.
target_answer: Each finding carries a CVSS v4.0 vector including threat and environmental metrics, an EPSS score snapshot, KEV membership and a reachability determination. KEV and high-likelihood reachable findings receive accelerated deadlines. Reachability-based deferrals are reviewed by someone other than the fixing engineer and are published to customers as VEX statements. Defects in structural control components (Strata access layer, Limen boundary, authorization core) are escalated one level because other controls depend on them.
intended_practice: Implement as part of the register in ANS-VUL-001.
customer_statement: Echelon intends to prioritize vulnerabilities using CVSS v4.0, EPSS and the CISA KEV catalog; this is not yet operating.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
residual_risks: Reachability analysis tooling for F# is immature; manual determinations may be wrong.

challenge.customer_intent: Customers want assurance that exploitable weaknesses are fixed before attackers use them.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Compromise through a known, exploited vulnerability left open because it was scored medium, or effort wasted on unreachable critical-scored findings.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: CVSS base score alone is a severity measure, not a risk measure; FIRST itself states CVSS is not a risk score. Severity-only SLAs over-prioritize unreachable issues and under-prioritize exploited medium issues.
challenge.legally_required: No law reviewed requires CVSS-based SLAs for a private vendor. KEV deadlines under BOD 26-04 (which replaced BOD 22-01 on 2026-06-10) bind federal civilian agencies only.
challenge.contractually_required: Many customer questionnaires and MSAs express SLAs by CVSS severity band; expect requests to commit to them.
challenge.historical_convention: Severity-banded SLAs (for example critical 15 or 30 days) are widespread industry convention.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Structural rules (SEC-DB-001, SEC-UI-002, SEC-EXEC-001) can make some dependency vulnerability classes unreachable, but only with scoped evidence that bypass is impossible.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Gate releases on KEV and on high EPSS plus reachable findings; keep CVSS bands as a floor.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Register with EPSS and KEV snapshots, reachability decisions and reviewer identity.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Hybrid: severity-band SLA as contractual ceiling, accelerated deadlines for KEV or high EPSS, documented reachability-based deferrals reviewed independently and disclosed via VEX.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, if reachability decisions and score snapshots are retained and sampled by an independent reviewer.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Reachability analysis is wrong or unverifiable for F#; EPSS data unavailable; customer contract fixes CVSS-only SLAs.
challenge.alternative_risks: Reachability determinations can be wrong and become an excuse for deferral; EPSS is probabilistic and can underweight targeted attacks on a niche financial platform.
supporting_arguments: KEV and EPSS directly reflect exploitation evidence.
VEX lets customers suppress non-affecting findings in their own tooling.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely if CVSS bands remain as ceilings; uncertain if CVSS bands are replaced entirely.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Auditors and banks often prefer a simple severity table they can test by sampling.
Targeted attacks against DAF platforms are unlikely to appear in EPSS, which models broad exploitation.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Remediation SLAs, verification and zero-day response
status_rationale: SOC2-016 requires recording fixes and retests; no SLA values have been set in any Echelon source.
target_answer: Proposed contractual ceilings: KEV or actively exploited, 7 days or less (mitigation within 48 hours); critical 15 days; high 30 days; medium 90 days; low at next scheduled release; measured from first detection or public disclosure, whichever is earlier, to deployed fix across all tenants. Closure requires rescan or regression test evidence. A zero-day playbook uses the SBOM index to answer exposure within hours. SLA performance is reported monthly with raw counts.
intended_practice: Set SLA values with counsel and early customers before signing, and enforce them via release gates.
customer_statement: Remediation timelines have not yet been adopted. Proposed targets can be discussed, and no SLA performance history exists because Unbound is not in production.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
residual_risks: Small-team capacity limits; simultaneous critical events could exceed SLA.
open_questions: What SLA values will Echelon commit to contractually, and has counsel reviewed them?

challenge.customer_intent: Bound the window of exposure for known weaknesses and make it contractually testable.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Known vulnerabilities remain exploitable for months.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Fixed-day SLAs measured from detection are testable but are routinely missed and quietly converted into exceptions; they measure process, not exposure.
challenge.legally_required: Not by statute for Echelon. PCI DSS Req 6.3.3 sets a one-month expectation for critical patches only where PCI DSS applies; it is not expected to apply to Unbound.
challenge.contractually_required: Common in bank and enterprise MSAs and security addenda.
challenge.historical_convention: Severity-banded SLAs measured in calendar days.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Rebuild-and-redeploy pipelines and small dependency surfaces shorten time to fix, making shorter SLAs achievable.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Release gate blocks on overdue findings; exception register expires automatically.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Exposure-window metric computed from register timestamps and deployment records, not from ticket closure.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Measure and commit to exposure window (from public disclosure to deployed fix across all tenants), not only ticket closure time.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, from deployment manifests joined to advisory publication dates.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: No reliable deployment manifest; manual deployments.
challenge.alternative_risks: Small team capacity may make aggressive commitments unachievable during simultaneous events.
supporting_arguments: Exposure window is what matters to the customer.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely as a supplement; customers still expect the familiar SLA table.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: A single-person or very small team cannot credibly promise 24x7 critical remediation without on-call depth.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Vulnerability exceptions and risk acceptance
status_rationale: The Secure Construction Standard enforcement model and SOC2-033 specify explicit, scoped, time-limited exceptions with accountable approval and compensating controls; formal adoption and implementation are unestablished.
target_answer: Exceptions are requested in a register, scoped to specific findings and releases, approved by an accountable reviewer other than the requester, accompanied by compensating controls, expire automatically and are re-reviewed; customers are told when an accepted risk affects a control they rely on. AI agents cannot create, approve, extend or close exceptions or suppressions.
intended_practice: Implement the exception register and gate integration with ANS-VUL-003.
customer_statement: Echelon's proposed standard requires time-limited, separately approved exceptions with compensating controls; the process is not yet operating.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
residual_risks: With a very small organization, separation between requester and approver may be impossible without an external reviewer.
open_questions: Who can accept risk on behalf of Echelon while the organization has few or no employees?

title: Vulnerability disclosure program and security.txt
status_rationale: No vulnerability disclosure policy, SECURITY.md or security.txt was located in Echelon repositories reviewed; no Echelon source proposes one.
target_answer: Echelon publishes a vulnerability disclosure policy aligned with ISO/IEC 29147 and 30111 covering all Echelon domains, products and open-source libraries, with good-faith safe harbor language reviewed by counsel, a monitored reporting address, security.txt files with current expiry on each domain, acknowledgment within 3 business days, triage within 10 business days, and coordinated disclosure.
current_practice: Unknown; no evidence located. No SECURITY.md or security.txt found in reviewed Echelon repositories.
intended_practice: Publish a VDP and security.txt before any public launch; add SECURITY.md to public Echelon repositories.
customer_statement: Echelon does not currently publish a vulnerability disclosure policy. Security reports can be sent to the company's general contact until one is established.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
open_questions: Does Echelon have a monitored security contact address?
Has counsel reviewed safe harbor language?

title: Bug bounty program
status_rationale: No Echelon source mentions a bug bounty. None is believed to exist; not verified.
target_answer: No paid bug bounty before production launch; a VDP with safe harbor plus independent penetration testing. Consider a private, invite-only bounty restricted to a dedicated test tenant with synthetic data once Unbound is in production and independently tested.
customer_statement: Echelon does not operate a bug bounty program.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

challenge.customer_intent: Continuous external scrutiny that finds what internal teams miss.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Bug bounties produce value for mature, internet-scale products; for a pre-production, low-traffic platform they mostly attract low-quality reports and require triage capacity Echelon does not have.
challenge.contractually_required: Rarely; usually asked as a preference.
challenge.historical_convention: Common among large SaaS vendors; uncommon for early-stage financial platforms.
challenge.continuous_evidence: A VDP intake log provides evidence of external engagement without paid bounties.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Start with a VDP plus safe harbor and targeted independent tests; add a private, invite-only bounty after production launch and independent test baseline.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes: published policy, intake log, independent test letters.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Large public user base or high-profile target status after launch.
challenge.alternative_risks: Fewer eyes on the product between independent tests.
supporting_arguments: Triage burden of public bounties is high relative to findings for small products.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely for most financial customers, who rank independent penetration testing above bounties.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Some enterprise questionnaires score the absence of a bounty negatively.
Bounties can find business-logic flaws that scheduled tests miss.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Customer notification of vulnerabilities and advisories
status_rationale: No customer vulnerability notification commitment exists; Unbound requirements define a notification catalog (UNB-RCN-PLT-002) but not vulnerability advisories specifically.
target_answer: Customers are notified within 2 business days when a vulnerability affecting their tenant or release is confirmed as exploitable and not yet fixed, with interim mitigations; advisories are issued after fixes; VEX statements are provided for non-affecting components; inquiries during public vulnerability events are answered within 1 business day from the SBOM index; subprocessor and platform vulnerabilities affecting the service are included.
intended_practice: Define advisory templates and notification commitments in the security addendum.
customer_statement: Vulnerability notification commitments have not yet been defined.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
open_questions: Will Echelon assign CVE identifiers for vulnerabilities in distributed libraries (for example via a CNA or GitHub advisories)?

title: Platform component patching and end-of-support management
status_rationale: Strata is pilot status and PostgreSQL 16 only; hosting is not selected. Rebuild-and-redeploy is a recommendation of this research, not an Echelon decision.
target_answer: Platform components (.NET runtime, PostgreSQL engine, container base images, OS) are patched by rebuilding immutable artifacts and redeploying through the gated pipeline; deployed versions are monitored against vendor security releases and support windows, with migration plans at least 6 months before end of support.
intended_practice: Adopt immutable build and deploy once hosting is selected.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet deployed; patching practices are planned, not operating.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
residual_risks: Strata supports PostgreSQL 16 only; a forced PostgreSQL major upgrade may depend on Strata changes.

title: AI agents in vulnerability remediation and AI tooling vulnerabilities
status_rationale: SOC2-017 requires AI agents to be attributable, bounded and monitored; Praxis provides provenance records for agent work, but no control specific to AI-authored security fixes exists.
target_answer: AI agents may draft fixes, but every AI-authored change is attributed to the agent and authorizing human, reviewed by a different principal, must pass security regression tests and cannot modify gates, findings or exceptions. Vulnerabilities in agent runtimes, model SDKs and tool integrations are inventoried and managed in the same register.
current_practice: Praxis records agent provenance for repository work (tooling exists, not operated for a production Echelon service). No security-specific review rule is enforced.
intended_practice: Extend Praxis gates to require independent review of agent-authored security fixes.
provable: Praxis provenance records for repository changes, which show agent attribution but not security verification.
customer_statement: Echelon uses AI agents in engineering and records their provenance in repository tooling; specific verification of AI-authored security fixes is planned, not operating.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
residual_risks: Reviewer may over-trust agent output; correlated errors if the same model family reviews its own work.
